bullets.title: Oracle FY26 Capex Misses High; Stock Drops 12%
bullets.body: Oracle FY26 capex came in at $55.7B vs. prior $50B guidance, with Q4 FY26 capex hitting $15.9B. The capex beat expectations to the upside, driving the stock down 12% as margin compression concerns dominate. Separately, OCI is described as pushing the frontier of AI infrastructure with Nvidia support.

bullets.title: NVIDIA: Lead Adopter of Advanced Packaging; Glass Substrate First Chips Ahead
bullets.body: Semiconductor analyst notes NVIDIA is the lead adopter of advanced process and packaging technologies, with first chips on glass substrates expected. Separately, the analyst has already modeled NVIDIA CPU uplift in a TAM expansion model. NVIDIA also received OpenAI's Industry AI Acceleration Award.

bullets.title: TSMC Pulls CoPoS Timeline Forward to 2028 from 2029
bullets.body: TSMC has accelerated its next-generation CoPoS (Copper on Polymer Substrate) advanced packaging technology by one year, now targeting 2028 instead of 2029. Sell-side had previously guided a 2029 timeline. Amkor is investing $650M in a 6-plant Gwangju campus expansion driven by a surge in TSMC orders.

bullets.title: AI Chip Price War Intensifying: Inference Costs Falling 5-10x Per Watt
bullets.body: Multiple next-gen accelerators coming online — Blackwell, TPU v7/v8, Trainium v3 — are cutting inference costs 5-10x on a per-watt basis, with software and algorithm optimizations adding another 2-5x reduction. The dynamic is driving accelerating AI price competition across hyperscalers and model providers.

bullets.title: OpenAI Considering Drastic Token Price Cuts vs. Anthropic; Margin Risk Flagged
bullets.body: WSJ reports OpenAI is weighing major cuts to token pricing as competition with Anthropic intensifies and some users balk at AI costs. Sources note OpenAI expects Anthropic to also reduce prices. A separate comment flags that price cuts could threaten OpenAI margins ahead of a potential IPO.

bullets.title: China's InP Export Delays Threatening AI Datacenter Supply Chain; AXTI Cited
bullets.body: Reuters reports U.S. officials have visited China multiple times urging resolution of indium phosphide (InP) export control delays. China's control over InP supply is flagged as a major risk to U.S. photonic chip makers and AI datacenter buildout. AXTI is identified as a key point of vulnerability in this supply chain.

bullets.title: Tech Sector Sees Record $10.8B Outflow; Major Names 5-24% Below ATH
bullets.body: Tech stocks experienced $10.8B in outflows last week, the largest ever recorded. Major names are trading well below all-time highs: TSLA -24%, AMZN/NVDA -15%, GOOGL -13%, AAPL -8%, with the S&P 500 off 5%.

bullets.title: Macro Bounce Setup: SPY/QQQ/SMH at Technical Confluence Support
bullets.body: Technical analyst flags a 'high probability bounce zone' where SPY, QQQ, and SMH converge at YTD low VWAP, 38.2% Fibonacci retrace of the rally, and the 50-day SMA. Another trader expects a rotation back into tech/AI 'within the next few days' for a relief rally, with ARM cited. US equity futures recovered: S&P futures +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.5%.

bullets.title: South Korea Semiconductor Exports Surge 206% YoY; KOSPI Recovers from 4.4% Drop
bullets.body: South Korea's June 1-10 exports hit a record $28.6B, with semiconductor exports surging 206% YoY. The KOSPI index erased an early 4.4% decline to trade positive amid extreme put/call ratio readings (highest since pre-GFC). Korean traders facing forced liquidations described as largest ever pace.

bullets.title: DRAM Supply Constrained vs. 'Infinite' Demand; Bull Case for MU
bullets.body: A fintwit account flags SK Hynix's plan to triple wafer capacity by 2034, noting supply remains constrained while demand is 'essentially infinite,' arguing this should drive prices higher. MSI's chairman confirms CPU shortages have been easing since Q2 with very strong server demand.

bullets.title: Vera Rubin AI Compute Supply Constrained Through Next Year
bullets.body: Sources report the allocation process for Vera Rubin (NVIDIA's next-gen platform) is underway and competitive, with AI compute supply expected to remain constrained through next year. Separately, rumors of 800 VDC production delay to 2028 are denied by Taiwan data center parts suppliers who report no delay notification from NVIDIA.

bullets.title: AWS Graviton at $6-7B ARR, Growing ~50% YoY; Higher Incremental Margins
bullets.body: Analyst estimates AWS Graviton as a ~$6-7B annualized run rate business growing ~50% YoY, representing ~5% of AWS's $150B+ revenue run rate, and carrying higher incremental margins. This underscores the CPU TAM expansion theme for custom silicon.

bullets.title: MSFT Restricts Internal Claude Use Over Data-Retention Concerns
bullets.body: MSFT has restricted internal use of Claude Fable due to data-retention concerns. BMO separately names Anthropic as a leading pure-play AI lab. Anthropic's $47B ARR claim is questioned by one commenter who notes it annualizes a one-time Feb-May agentic spend surge.

bullets.title: AI Server Demand Tightening High-End MLCC Supply; Taiwan Firms Exploring China Alt
bullets.body: AI servers and high-voltage EVs are driving a demand surge for high-end MLCCs, tightening global supply and lengthening lead times. Some Taiwanese supply-chain players are now exploring China sourcing as an alternative, a development with potential supply chain and geopolitical implications.

bullets.title: Photonics Sector: Capacity Sold Out, Thesis Intact Despite Pullback
bullets.body: A fintwit trader notes the photonics sector has a 'monstrous TAM,' is fully sold out on capacity, and the recent valuation pullback is creating a buying opportunity. Taiwan airlines reported strong AI cargo demand in May: China Airlines AI cargo up 53.5% YoY, Eva Air up 41.5% YoY — implying sustained demand for photonics-linked components.

bullets.title: US Inflation Macro: Core CPI Possibly Distorted; $1.3T Interest Expense Record
bullets.body: Commentary flags that Core CPI may be artificially depressed by import price deflation, masking embedded domestic services inflation. US interest expense on public debt hit a record $1.3T over the last 12 months, with US consumer prices up 4.5%/year over 5 years. A 14% inflation premium since 2020 cited as reason monetary policy should remain restrictive.

bullets.title: SiriAI (iOS 27) Competitive Check: Superior On-Device Semantic Search vs. Gemini
bullets.body: A chip/tech analyst tested new SiriAI for half a day and found its semantic search is 'the best on-device' experienced, though still prefers Gemini for broad knowledge queries. AAPL's AI assistant may be gaining functional credibility, with capabilities expected to improve further.

bullets.title: MRVL: $1.1M Bearish Put Sweep Signals Institutional Short Into September
bullets.body: Options flow shows a $1.1M put sweep on MRVL with September expiration, interpreted as bearish institutional positioning ahead of that date.

bullets.title: JPM: AI Infrastructure Costs 'Out of Control'; $1.8T in Hidden Liabilities
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags AI infrastructure bills as spiraling out of control. A separate commentary highlights ~$1.8T in off-balance-sheet liabilities across the tech sector, including $1T in undisclosed purchase commitments and $0.8T in future lease obligations, with SPVs used to obscure visibility.

bullets.title: Macro: Market Pullback to 50-Day MA Seen as Healthy; Bull Market Wall of Worry
bullets.body: One trader argues the market weakness and revisiting the 50-day moving average is constructive for sustained bull market advances, characterizing the current pullback as 'building a wall of worry.' Separately, widespread crash expectations are seen as reducing the probability of a sudden disorderly decline.
